sample_unit: simulated OHCA scenarios and 911 dispatcher-assisted calls

links.outcome: Adherence of general AI models to guideline-based CPR instruction criteria in simulated cardiac arrest scenarios
links.effect: Models met 89.7% of minimally viable criteria (Gemini 79.4%) but only 69.8% of maximally effective criteria (Llama 61.3%); purpose-built agent reached 100% on both in the same scenarios.
links.quote: In simulated OHCA scenarios among 6 widely available AI models, the models achieved 89.7% (95% CI, 84.8%-93.2%) of minimally viable criteria, ranging from 79.4% (95% CI, 63.2%-89.7%) for Gemini to 97.1% (95% CI, 85.1%-99.5%) for Grok and Claude.

links.outcome: AI agent adherence to CPR instruction criteria compared with 911 dispatchers on real calls
links.effect: Agent achieved 100% minimally viable and 98.9% maximally effective adherence, absolute improvements of 15.5 points (P = .02) and 36.1 points (P < .001) over dispatchers (84.5% and 62.8%).
links.quote: In a retest using 911 calls, the agent achieved 100% (95% CI, 88.6%-100%) adherence to minimally viable and 98.9% (95% CI, 94.0%-99.8%) adherence to maximally effective criteria, representing absolute improvements of 15.5 percentage points (95% CI, 2.1-27.4 percentage points; P = .02) and 36.1 percentage points (95% CI, 27.2-44.3 percentage points; P < .001) over dispatchers (84.5%; 95% CI, 73.1%-91.6% and 62.8%; 95% CI, 55.0%-70.0%, respectively).

unlisted_practices: Purpose-built, guideline-constrained AI agent for emergency bystander CPR instruction

screen.reason: The study evaluates the baseline capability of LLMs and develops a specialized agent (ChatCPR) to provide bystander CPR instructions using simulated scenarios and retrospective 911 calls, measuring guideline adherence without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
